extracted.intended_audience: federal court, litigators, and parties (news organizations) involved in AP v. INS injunction litigation; legal staff and journalists interested in agency practices
extracted.subtask_description: Replying affidavits filed by The Associated Press in the United States District Court (S.D.N.Y.) rebutting defendant affidavits on topics such as animus, 'clean hands', alleged interchange of dispatches, and customary news‑service practices. The documents state AP rules, practices, and specific factual denials (e.g., Lusitania reporting, Syracuse events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial news entitlement / scope of supplied news
rubrics_metrics.description: It was the distinct understanding that Cushing was to furnish to The Associated Press only the news of Cleveland and vicinage, to which it was entitled under the by-laws of The Associated Press, and not the news of any other news distributing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiant states this was the specific engagement term (April 1916) and frames it as a governing limit on what local correspondents may supply to AP; if news from other agencies had been offered it 'would have been refused and would not have been used.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal policy for non-member/other-agency news
rubrics_metrics.description: If the news of other news distributing agencies had been offered, under the rules in force in my division, it would have been refused and would not have been used by us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a departmental rule/practice: offers of dispatches from other agencies are to be refused rather than accepted into AP service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using dispatches of non-members
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees of this service are prohibited from taking or using as Associated Press despatches the despatches or stories of other news agencies or of newspapers not members of The Associated Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiant (Chief of News Department) asserts this rule has been 'strictly enforced' during his entire service; used to rebut allegations that AP reproduced or relied on competitors' dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to report hints/tips for independent investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees of the Associated Press are under instructions to immediately report to their next superior rumors or hints of news occurrences in order that they may be investigated through our own efforts and original stories thereon prepared for the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the internal workflow: tips are reported so AP can investigate and produce original coverage rather than adopt another agency's copy; used to distinguish legitimate newsgathering from illicit appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interchange policy between competing services via member newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: The understanding has been that there was to be no interchange of news between the two services (Associated Press and International News Service) through the Cleveland News office; positive instructions were issued by the managing editor that there should be no interchange of news dispatches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple Cleveland News employees testify to no instruction/understanding to supply INS dispatches to AP; presented to defeat 'clean hands' and interchange allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification before distribution (confirm primary source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before distributing a report (example: sinking of the Lusitania), the Associated Press confirmed the report by telephone with the Cunard Steamship Company and then sent out a bulletin stating the information as an 'unconfirmed report'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example used (May 7, 1915) to show AP practice of confirming with authoritative sources before broad distribution; supports the standard of independent verification prior to dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of operators to prevent eavesdropping / no colocated operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The uniform practice of The Associated Press is not to permit its correspondents or operators receiving or sending its news to perform these functions in the same room with the correspondent or telegraph operator of any other news-agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiants concede exceptions (Syracuse courthouse room) where operators were colocated and explain why that was unusual; standard is physical separation to avoid 'tips' by hearing other wires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reproduce competitor dispatches without original investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no instance recalled where a dispatch has been used by The Associated Press reproducing dispatches carried by other agencies or newspapers not members of AP without originally investigating and ascertaining the facts through our own sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as a long-standing practice/precedent; used to rebut claims that AP simply republished INS dispatches without verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and record transparency for local correspondents
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been the practice to send a check covering the salary and expenses of all local correspondents to one chief correspondent, who then pays correspondents in currency; such payment in currency was not in any way to conceal the arrangement and appears on organization records and weekly disbursement reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit explains administrative practice to counter insinuations that cash payments were intended to hide relationships or improper arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for rebutting alleged animus in employee departures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal of claimed 'animus' rests on showing voluntary resignation and evidence of pleasant relations at time of resignation (example: letter stating 'you are one of the best telegraphers we have had' and offering re-employment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiants present contemporaneous letters and testimony about working relations to negate allegations that former employees left with animus against INS or AP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden to identify source/tip allegations with documentary/time-stamped records
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiants examine file messages and timing (e.g., record of a single brief message 'Can I do anything on explosion? Am after Draper' at 3:28 p.m.) and assert absence of any message from particular persons in AP files; implication that allegations should be supported by contemporaneous records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in rebuttal to show claimed tips or transmissions (e.g., on Lusitania or Solvay explosion) do not appear in AP's message logs; emphasizes reliance on contemporaneous documentary evidence in adjudicating claims.
